engineering.intro: A SwiftUI app I built by directing Claude Code across more than 100 pull requests, with a release pipeline that goes from a git tag to TestFlight on its own.

facts.v: unit tests gating every agent session
commits in the first ten weeks

points.title: Hand-written SQLite, no ORM
points.text: Repositories are actors over SQLite in WAL mode. Writes are diffed and carry revisions, timestamps and tombstones, so the store is ready for sync before sync exists. Schema migrations are versioned.

points.title: A backend that fits in one file
points.text: A Cloudflare Worker proxies TMDB so the API token never ships in the app. It allow-lists paths, caches for four hours and rate-limits each IP.

points.title: Awards data pipeline
points.text: A weekly job joins Wikidata award records to TMDB ids and rebuilds the bundled catalog of Oscar, BAFTA and Emmy history.

points.title: Tag-driven releases
points.text: Pushing a tag archives the app and uploads to TestFlight with screenshots and preview video. The phased App Store rollout can start and halt based on Sentry crash-free rates.

points.title: Marketing as code
points.text: The screenshots and clips on this page are recorded by a script that drives the simulator through a scripted tour, then frames the output.

points.title: Watching production
points.text: Sentry for crashes, anonymous TelemetryDeck events sent with plain URLSession, a daily TMDB contract check, and a weekly digest that files a GitHub issue.
